To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
zero temperature limit measures are supported on the zero-level-set of the potential and that the selection mechanism is mediated by evanescence of the entropic contributions to the free energy.

(1) the zero-temperature limit of a minimal energy state of a finite-dimensional interacting corpus is the measure that assigns zero mass to the interior and assigns equal masses to the zero-level-set of the interaction potential and to the complement of this set; (2) the selection of a specific measure in the set of all zero-mass measures is mediated by the entropic contribution of the system.
the zero temperature limit for interacting corpora is mediated by evanescing entropic contributions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the zero temperature limit in statistical mechanics.
the zero temperature limit in the theory of interacting corpora (i.e. objects with a finite number of degrees of freedom).
the zero temperature limit for interacting corpora, that is, for systems with a finite number of degrees of freedom such as articulated rods.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in the limit of zero temperature, a minimal free energy configuration of a corpus is a measure supported on the zero-level-set of the interaction potential, and that, if the corpus is not too rigid, this measure is supported on the global minimum of the potential.
the zero-temperature limit of interacting corporae is a selection of zero-level sets of the interaction potential, mediated by evanesent entropic effects.
the zero temperature limit is not a well-defined concept for a system with finite degrees of freedom, and the limit is not unique.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the zero temperature limit for interacting corpora is a zero-level-set measure.
we characterize the zero temperature limits of minimal free energies states for interacting corporal objects, that is objects with finitey many degrees of freedom such as articulated rods or chains.

we have shown that the zero-temperature limit of the free energy of a system of N interacting particles, with interaction energy of the order of the inverse of N, is a measure supported on the zero-level set of the interaction potential, provided that this level set is nonempty.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the limit of infinite temperature, interacting corpora tend to minimize the interaction potential.
, in the zero temperature limit, the minimal free energy states are not necessarily concentrated on the global minimizer of the energy functional.
the zero-temperature limit of an interacting system is not necessarily a point, but a measure.
